kotlin-rule-gate._comment: Enforces rules/android.md / rules/lean.md on agent writes to *.kt: no // or /* */ comments (KDoc allowed), no literal strings in user-facing Compose params, no raw hex colors outside :core:designsystem. PreToolUse rather than PostToolUse because the PostToolUse payload carries no toolCall, so it cannot know the target file. Fails open on any error or unrecognised argument shape. Verified: 13/13 fixtures, 0 false positives across the 90 files in CodebaseCompose. Pass verdict is 'ask' (normal approval flow preserved); flip PASS_DECISION in rule_gate.py to 'allow' to auto-approve clean Kotlin writes.

root-write-guard._comment: Re-homes the 'orchestrator never writes code' invariant, which `mainAgent` cannot carry: `agy --agent <name>` does not load a custom agent in CLI 1.1.22, so orchestrator.md's empty write-tool list enforces nothing. This denies writes to SOURCE files (kt/kts/java/xml/gradle/py/sh/ps1/json/toml/properties) when the calling conversation is the ROOT session, and passes them for delegates -- so the human's session must dispatch the `executor` subagent instead of editing. Docs, notes and plans are never gated; the invariant is about code. Root/delegate is decided by scanning sibling brain dirs for a parent's 'Created the following subagents' record naming this conversationId -- directional on purpose, because a child names its parent when reporting back and a plain substring test misreads every parent as a delegate. Delegate verdicts cache to .agents/state/write_guard/ (~15ms cold across 505 brain dirs, 0.11ms cached); root is deliberately NOT cached so a late parent flush can still flip it. Fails open on any error, unknown arg shape, or missing conversationId. ENABLED BY DEFAULT: it is the enforcement half of the delegation rule in AGENTS.md at the project ROOT (moved there from rules/orchestrate.md on 2026-08-28 -- rule files did not reliably reach the turn, and this is the one rule whose failure is silent), which states the same invariant as always-on prompt context. It is stricter than the original invariant and will block your own one-line fixes. Escape hatch without editing config: `python .agents/hooks/write_guard.py --off` (and --on, --status). Verified 33/33 fixtures plus 3 real conversation ids. Scoped to the project root, so an agent's own scratch space under ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<id>/scratch/ is never gated, and goals.json is exempt (it is ultrawork step 2). UNVERIFIED: how Antigravity combines two PreToolUse verdicts when this and kotlin-rule-gate both match a write -- check before trusting it in anger.

ultrawork-intent-gate._comment: Turns the literal word 'ultrawork' (or 'ultra work' / 'ulw') in a user prompt into an injected directive that activates .agents/skills/ultrawork/SKILL.md. PreInvocation carries NO prompt text, so the transcript is the only source. Cheap by construction: the transcript is append-only, so the hook stores a byte offset per conversationId and scans only what was appended -- the common case is a stat plus a 256-byte head check (file identity; size alone cannot detect rotation), and only the first invocation of a conversation reads the whole file. Fires at most once per triggering prompt (records are fingerprinted on created_at + request text) and at most 8 times per conversation. Three deliberate stand-downs: the trigger is matched ONLY inside <USER_REQUEST> (the <ADDITIONAL_METADATA> block inlines whole skill bodies for slash commands, so matching there would fire on any skill that mentions the word); nothing is injected when the record shows the platform already activated the skill ('invoked the (ultrawork) skill' -- typing /ultrawork loads it natively, since skills are Antigravity's slash-command mechanism); and records carrying the hook's own <ultrawork-mode> marker are skipped so an injection cannot re-trigger the gate. Keying on a literal word also scopes it to the main session for free -- a subagent's task prompt cannot contain the trigger unless the orchestrator put it there. Fuzzy activation ('do this properly') is left to the skill's description and Antigravity's semantic discovery; a regex for intent would fire on prose about rigour. Fails open (prints {}) on any error. Escape hatch without editing config: `python .agents/hooks/intent_gate.py --off` (also --on, --status, --print-directive, --scan <transcript>). Verified: 36 fixtures. NOTE: this is the second PreInvocation handler alongside scrcpy-daemon, so each LLM call now pays two Python startups (~50ms each); if a third ever appears, merge them into one dispatcher.

stop-verifier._comment: Holds a registered goal loop open until its goals hold. Inert unless the stopping conversation OWNS a loop under .agents/state/loop/ -- so it is opt-in by construction (someone ran `loop.py create-goals`) and cannot fight subagents, which do not own their parent's loop. Brakes before verification: hard-stops on the real terminationReason enum (ERROR/USER_CANCELED/MAX_INVOCATIONS/MAX_FORCED_INVOCATIONS/MAX_TOKEN_BUDGET_EXCEEDED/HALTED_STEP/TERMINAL_CUSTOM_HOOK -- payload values are the TERMINATION_REASON_* enum minus its prefix, e.g. NO_TOOL_CALL, NOT the docs' 'model_stop'); defers while fullyIdle is false; caps resumes at 2 per goal (1 after compaction) and 6 per session; marks the loop stuck and stops when the LEDGER did not advance across a resume; backs off exponentially after failed checkpoints; and honours the skill's own three-consecutive-failures rule. Verification validates the RECORD, never re-runs the work: a recorded non-zero exit code under a 'complete' goal, a missing evidence artifact, or goals.json drifting from the ledger each block the stop -- because a Stop hook running Gradle would cost 30-90s against a 30s timeout. Fails open (prints {"decision":"stop"}, the value probe.py proved safe) on any error. ~50ms per Stop with no loop registered (Python startup), ~70ms worst case with a 6MB transcript. Escape hatch without editing config: `python .agents/hooks/stop_verifier.py --off` (also --on, --status, --clear [--session X]). Verified: 52 fixtures including the acceptance case (no constructable case resumes more than twice), plus a live two-goal session (CLI 1.1.22) where an unfinished goal was resumed exactly once and then permitted, and an unsatisfiable goal was closed out as `failed` on the record rather than ground on. The block reaches the agent as a SYSTEM_MESSAGE prefixed 'Stop hook blocked termination: '.

omo-port-probe._comment: Contract probe. Q1/Q3 answered 2026-08-27 -- findings recorded in docs/omo-port/MAPPING.md. Left disabled rather than deleted: re-enable to answer Q7 (named-agent invoke_subagent shape) by running one delegation to a named .agents/agents/* agent. CWD is confirmed to be .agents/, so the '|| python hooks/...' fallback is redundant.

scrcpy-daemon._comment: Owns the scrcpy-cli daemon so the agent never runs `daemon start`/`daemon stop` itself. Brings the daemon up on the first LLM call of a conversation (ALWAYS_START=True in scrcpy_daemon.py; set it False to start only when the transcript shows device work). Idempotent via a per-conversationId marker, so the ~50 PreInvocations in a session cost one marker check each. A 60s negative cache avoids re-probing when no device is attached. Stop is refcounted by conversationId so a finishing subagent cannot kill a daemon its parent is still using, and a daemon started by hand outside the agent is never stopped. PreInvocation/Stop only -- a PreToolUse hook on run_command would have to return a decision for every shell command. Verified on a Pixel 7a: detached spawn, non-blocking, refcount, and cleanup all confirmed.
